title: Blood test could gauge if a baby has a dangerous infection in 15 minutes | New Scientist
description: Feverish babies in hospital are often assumed to have a serious bacterial infection and are treated with antibiotics. But a test that gauges whether the infection is bacterial or viral, which tend to be milder, could prevent unnecessary drug use
author: Michael Marshall

title: Virtual green spaces and classical music reduce blood pressure in hospital | New Scientist
description: Watching a river flow via a virtual-reality headset while listening to classical music seems to quickly bring people's blood pressure down from a dangerously high level in hospital
author: Chris Simms

title: Is China catching up to the US and SpaceX on reusable rockets? | New Scientist
description: The next space race is not about making rockets faster, bigger or more capacious, but about reusing them reliably and cheaply. The US is well ahead, but can China catch up?
author: Matthew Sparkes

title: Mathematician discovers rare eight-faced shape | New Scientist
description: It isn't easy to demonstrate that a new geometric shape can actually exist in the real world, but one researcher argues that the genus-3 polyhedron can
author: Chris Stokel-Walker

title: Dogs pay more attention to consonants than vowels when we speak | New Scientist
description: Hooking up dogs to non-invasive EEG monitors has helped identify exactly which component of human speech the animals are most attuned to
author: James Woodford

title: Copying others can help young orangutans build a broad diet | New Scientist
description: Orangutans spend more than eight years learning how to cope on their own, and now we have a clearer idea of how they work out which foods to incorporate into their diet
author: Christa Lesté-Lasserre
